**Chapter 11**

**11.1 Aromatic Hydrocarbons**

The word 'Aromatic' is taken from the Greek word Aroma which means scent or fragrance. This was so named because the first aromatic compounds were sweet-smelling. Benzene (C6H6) or Naphthalene (C10H8) is the instance of Aromatic Hydrocarbons.

The aromatic compounds are generally 5, 6 or 7 membered co-planar cyclic compounds. It has alternative double bonds that means there is a carbon-carbon single bond and a then carbon-carbon double bond.

**11.2 Unsaturated Closed Chain Hydrocarbon: Cyclopropane**

Cyclopropane is a three-membered ring of carbon atoms with one double bond. It is a highly reactive molecule due to its strained ring structure.

**11.3 Unsaturated Closed Chain Hydrocarbon: Cyclobutane**

Cyclobutane is a four-membered ring of carbon atoms with one double bond. It is a relatively stable molecule compared to cyclopropane.

**11.4 Saturated Closed Chain Hydrocarbon: Cyclopropane**
